text: Please open the window and welcome the morning.
choices: Open the window to greet the morning.
Close the door and go to sleep.
Make dinner before going outside.

text: Today is a fresh start.
choices: Yesterday must happen again.
Today is a new beginning.
The day has already ended.

text: A small step can begin a great day.
choices: You must do everything at once.
Small actions never matter.
One little action can start a good day.

text: A warm cup of tea can make a quiet morning feel special.
choices: Tea can make a calm morning feel pleasant.
Tea makes every morning noisy.
A cup of tea is always cold.

text: She takes a short walk before starting work.
choices: She walks after work is finished.
She takes a brief walk before working.
She stays home all day.

text: Bring an umbrella because rain is expected this afternoon.
choices: It will be sunny all afternoon.
The umbrella is broken.
Rain may come later today.

text: The plant grew new leaves after it received water and sunlight.
choices: Water and sunlight helped the plant grow.
The plant lost all its leaves.
The plant grew without light or water.

text: He listened carefully before sharing his idea.
choices: He spoke before anyone else.
He paid attention before speaking.
He forgot to share his idea.

text: The bakery on the corner opens before sunrise.
choices: The corner bakery starts work very early.
The bakery stays closed until the evening.
The corner shop only sells umbrellas.

text: A neighbor left fresh flowers by the front door.
choices: A neighbor took the flowers away.
Someone placed new flowers near the entrance.
The front door was painted bright red.

text: She packed her bag the night before to stay calm.
choices: She forgot her bag at the office.
She left home without any plans.
She prepared her bag early so the morning would be calm.

text: The train was quiet, so he read a few pages.
choices: He read a little because the train was peaceful.
The train was too loud for reading.
He slept through the whole journey.

text: Soft rain tapped on the window all morning.
choices: A loud storm shook the house.
A gentle rain fell against the glass.
The sun burned brightly all day.

text: We ate breakfast on the balcony in the sunshine.
choices: We had dinner in the basement.
We skipped breakfast and stayed in bed.
Breakfast was outside in the sun.

text: The kettle whistled, and she made a pot of tea.
choices: She prepared tea when the kettle sounded.
The kettle was broken and silent.
She poured cold juice into a bowl.

text: He watered the herbs on the windowsill every day.
choices: He never remembered the herbs.
The windowsill herbs get water daily.
The herbs grew in a distant field.

text: The library opens at nine and closes at six.
choices: The library is open all night.
The library never opens on weekdays.
The library is open during the day.

text: A warm scarf is useful on a chilly morning.
choices: A scarf helps when the morning is cold.
A scarf is needed in the hottest weather.
A scarf is only good for the summer.

text: The children walked to school together, laughing along the way.
choices: The children traveled to school alone and silent.
The kids went to school as a happy group.
The school was closed, so everyone stayed home.

text: After stretching, she felt more awake and ready.
choices: Stretching made her very sleepy.
She felt tired and refused to move.
Stretching helped her feel alert.

text: The market was busy with people buying fruit.
choices: Many shoppers were buying fruit at the market.
The market was empty and silent.
People were selling shoes at the market.

text: He turned off the lights to save energy.
choices: He turned on every light in the house.
He switched off the lights so less power was used.
He left the lights burning all day.

text: A short pause can help you think more clearly.
choices: You should never stop to think.
Pausing always makes the day longer.
Taking a brief break can clear your mind.

text: The river was calm, and a single boat floated by.
choices: One boat drifted along the still river.
Many boats raced across rough water.
The river had dried up completely.

text: She hung the laundry outside because the day was sunny.
choices: She hung the laundry in the snow.
Sunny weather let her dry the clothes outdoors.
She refused to wash any clothes.

text: The old bridge connects the town to the hills.
choices: The bridge is brand new and unused.
The town has no way to the hills.
A bridge links the town with the hills.

text: He read the instructions twice before starting.
choices: He checked the directions two times first.
He began without looking at anything.
He threw the instructions away unread.

text: The cat slept in a patch of warm sunlight.
choices: The cat ran through the cold rain.
The cat napped where the sun was warm.
The cat sat in a dark closet.

text: It is easier to wake up when the room is bright.
choices: Darkness makes waking up easier.
Brightness makes everyone fall asleep.
Bright light makes waking up simpler.

text: The musician practiced a quiet tune before breakfast.
choices: A musician played soft music before eating.
The musician refused to play at all.
A loud concert began after midnight.

text: We planted tomato seeds, and soon small shoots appeared.
choices: The seeds turned to stone overnight.
Tiny plants came up soon after we planted the seeds.
We never planted anything this year.

text: The bus was late, so she decided to walk.
choices: The bus arrived early, so she rode it.
She took a taxi to the moon.
Because the bus was delayed, she went on foot.

text: He saved a seat for a tired friend.
choices: He kept a chair free for his weary friend.
He sat in every chair himself.
He told his friend to stand outside.

text: The soup needs a few more minutes on the stove.
choices: The soup is finished and cold.
The soup is not ready yet.
The stove broke before cooking started.

text: Leaves drifted down from the trees onto the path.
choices: The path was swept perfectly clean.
The trees grew taller overnight.
Leaves fell from the trees and covered the path.

text: A good habit grows from repeating a small action.
choices: Repeating a little action can build a good habit.
One huge effort builds every habit.
Habits form without any action at all.

text: The fog lifted slowly as the sun climbed higher.
choices: The fog became thicker at noon.
The mist cleared as the sun rose.
The sun disappeared behind the fog forever.

text: She wrote a thank you note to her teacher.
choices: She ignored her teacher completely.
She wrote an angry letter to a stranger.
She sent her teacher a note of thanks.

text: The garden smells sweet after a morning shower.
choices: A little rain makes the garden smell pleasant.
The garden smells terrible in the rain.
The garden is covered in sand.

text: He folded the map and put it in his pocket.
choices: He tore the map into pieces.
He tucked the folded map into his pocket.
He left the map open on a bench.

text: The street was calm until the delivery truck arrived.
choices: The street was loud before the truck came.
The delivery truck never reached the street.
A delivery truck broke the street's calm.

text: Warm bread tastes best with a little butter.
choices: Bread is especially nice warm with butter.
Cold stones taste best with butter.
Butter makes bread impossible to eat.
